input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 reverses our required ownership direction. Type II Materials expressly include works "created during the Service performance period," IBM owns them, and Type II is the default where nothing is specified — so deliverables we pay for default to IBM ownership with only an irrevocable licence limited to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" (no modification or sublicensing rights). Conversely, where we do own Type I Materials, we must grant IBM an irrevocable worldwide licence to distribute them externally and to authorise others to do the same, which lets IBM exploit our work product beyond performing the Services. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain ownership of our Content, Customer Components and data (11.6 only allocates responsibility; 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). The redline makes Type I the default, confines IBM ownership to pre-existing/generic IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back covering IBM IP embedded in deliverables, narrows IBM's licence in our Materials to performing the Services, and adds a Customer Data/no-joint-ownership provision.

proposal.summary: Make Customer-ownership (Type I) the default for Materials created for us, limit IBM-owned Type II Materials to pre-existing/generic IP with a broader licence back, restrict IBM's licence in Customer-owned Materials to performing the Services, and confirm we retain all rights in Content and Customer Components with no joint ownership.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for: Materials created for us during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned), with IBM retaining only its pre-existing and generic IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back that is not limited to internal Enterprise use, and IBM's licence in our Materials limited to performing the Services. We have also confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components and that nothing is jointly owned or assigned to IBM. If IBM cannot move the default, we can accept IBM ownership of generic tools and know-how provided we receive the broad licence in paragraph (c) and the ownership confirmation in paragraph (e).

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: distribute (internally and externally) copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials; and 2. the right to authorize others to do any of the same.
ops.newText: distribute internally copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials, in each case solely as necessary to perform the Services for Customer; and 2. the right to authorize its Subcontractors to do any of the same solely for that purpose.

ops.oldText: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: c. Type II Materials are those that preexist the Service performance period, or that consist of IBM's generic tools, know-how or platform components, in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, prepare derivative works based on, and distribute copies of Type II Materials, and to sublicense the foregoing rights to its Enterprise and to contractors acting on its behalf, in each case for Customer's business purposes, including any Type II Materials incorporated in or necessary to use Type I Materials.

ops.text: e. Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content, the Customer Components, and all other data Customer or its Services Recipients provide or generate through the Services. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content, the Customer Components, such data, or any Type I Materials, and no Materials, work product, or data will be jointly owned by the parties.
